l: Oz, The Cowardly Lion of Oz
s: Oz is a fairy kingdom, magic country, and wonderful land whose capital is the Emerald City. Ruled by Ozma, with Glinda as its good sorceress and the Wizard of Oz among its figures, it is a place where nothing can really be killed. It has an Emerald clock in the royal palace, fairy forests, many wizards, unusual people and animals, and numerous countries and regions, including the Munchkin Country, Gillikin Kingdom, Winkie Country, Quadling Country, Skyland, Un, and Mudge. Its events are recorded in the Magic Record Book. The records begin by presenting Oz as the setting of continuing stories and explain its protective magic when the Cowardly Lion is cut in two. Travelers then move through its strange forests and countries toward the Emerald City, encountering its marvels and peoples. Oz's magic cannot at first restore the petrified Cowardly Lion, but he is revived through tears. The account ends with Ozma making Oz the permanent home of Notta, Bob Up, and Snorer, while Notta performs shows and Mustafa's stone lions are displayed throughout the land.

l: Cowardly Lion, The Cowardly Lion of Oz
s: The Cowardly Lion is a dear, old, jolly, famous talking lion of Oz: once king of the forest creatures, beloved as a celebrity, Dorothy’s friend and favorite, and an adventurer who spends most of his time in the Emerald City after traveling there with Dorothy. He is kind-hearted, protective, and celebrated for saving Oz and performing many brave deeds, yet his lasting cowardice makes him tremble, want to flee danger, fear guns, and long to feel brave. Despite this fear, he fights enemies until overcoming them and protects others. Seeking courage, he leaves the Emerald City for Munchkin Country intending to find and swallow Oz’s bravest man. He meets Notta Bit More and Bob Up, instead escorts them toward the Emerald City, and repeatedly guards them: facing crowds, fighting the Uns, pulling them back to safety, rescuing them after a storm, and traveling tied to Notta. Blue feathers in his mane lead him to recognize that his plan to eat a brave person was unwise and unfair. When he learns Notta refused to capture him, he abandons the plan and decides he would rather remain a coward than gain courage that way. Mustafa pursues him, intending to imprison him in Mudge with a gold collar and chain. After danger, separation, and travel with Crunch to help Notta and Bob, he is captured and brought before 9,999 lions. He is turned to stone while preparing to fight, but Dorothy’s tears restore him; he prefers being a Cowardly Lion to being a stone lion. Reunited with Notta and welcomed by Dorothy, he ends among friends in Oz, still cowardly but consistently brave when others need him.

l: Mustafa, The Cowardly Lion of Oz
s: Mustafa of Mudge is the blue-whiskered, cross-eyed, wicked monarch and ruler of Mudge. Wealthy from selling stone lions, he keeps 9,999 and a half lions in a royal reservation and cares for them more than for his subjects; they are also the only thing that makes him laugh. Bored by kingship, he becomes determined to add the rarer Cowardly Lion to his collection after seeing him in a lion book. He intends to imprison the Lion in Mudge, fitting him with a jeweled collar and heavy gold chain and using him as a fighter against his other lions. Mustafa governs through orders and the dreadful power of his magic ring. He commands Notta and Bob Up to travel toward the Emerald City and capture the Cowardly Lion, providing food and directions while threatening to turn them blue and immobilize them if they disobey. When they fail, he activates the ring and does so. He watches the ring almost constantly, and his steady squinting leaves him permanently cross-eyed. He also enchants Notta and the Cowardly Lion, binding them by rope and making the ring summon them if they travel wrongly. When the Cowardly Lion reaches Mudge, Mustafa welcomes him, has Guards collar and chain him, and orders him into the lion enclosure to fight 9,999 lions. Yet Crunch attacks the enclosure, and Mustafa is petrified with terror. He loses the Cowardly Lion, his other lions, and his ring; at Ozma's command he surrenders the ring and shuffles mournfully back to his tent.

l: Mudge, The Cowardly Lion of Oz
s: Mudge is a hot, dry, blue desert country and kingdom in the southwestern part of the Munchkin country of Oz, also called a city and the land of the Mudgers. Surrounded by the royal lion reservation, it is subject to the lion tax, which its people resent. Mustafa rules Mudge; its borders are closed to outsiders, and a blue book dropped by Glinda forbids Mudgers to leave, under a law that says those who do lose their heads. Mudge protects a privately patented magic transformation formula and contains the blue-striped tent, the royal tent, and Mustafa’s tent. Notta first brings himself and Bobbie there, and later sends the Uns there with “Udge! Budge! Come to Mudge!” Mustafa cages twenty Uns and keeps 9,999 lions enclosed, intending to hold the Cowardly Lion once he enters. As travelers move toward Mudge, the Cowardly Lion faces grave danger and Crunch carries him there. In the end, Ozma orders petrified Crunch to stand in Mudge forever as a monument to Mustafa’s greediness and folly.

l: Scarecrow, The Cowardly Lion of Oz
s: Scarecrow, a living cotton scarecrow and Emerald City celebrity, has family and plays checkers with Princess Ozma. He travels with Ozma to Mudge and recklessly reaches Mustafa's enclosure as lions spring at Cowardly Lion.

l: Snorer, The Cowardly Lion of Oz
s: Snorer, also known as Nickadoodle or Nick, is an unusual huge, ridiculous pink bird and crow from the Isle of Un. His long curved blue beak, curly nose, and radio ear let him hear his own explosive, habitual snoring, which wakes him and often makes communication difficult. A faithful, devoted companion of Notta, Bob Up, and Nickadoodle’s friends, he lives with Notta and Bob in Notta’s tent and loves Notta. He knows that the Flyaboutabus is the means of escape from Un. He joins Notta, Bob, and the Cowardly Lion, cuts the vehicle’s rope, pilots and guides it, finds food, and helps restore Notta and Bob to normal. Through crashes, storms, falls, and mountain travel, he repeatedly protects or carries Bob and tries to save Notta, though exhaustion makes him sleep and snore. He helps reach the Emerald City, where Tik Tok seizes him. Later he wants to return to America to patent his nose and teach people to snore properly, but remains in Oz with Notta and Bob Up, helping with their surprising shows.

l: Dorothy, The Cowardly Lion of Oz
s: Dorothy is a little girl from Kansas, a celebrity in the Emerald City, and an old, faithful friend of the Cowardly Lion. Though Notta hopes she can help return him to the United States, she prefers Oz to returning to Kansas. Bob Up finds her reading in the Emerald City gardens; she mistakes Notta for a witch, drenches him, and calls for help. She later joins the party at Mudge, mourns the petrified Lion, and her tears help restore him to life.

l: the two cowardly lion hunters, The Cowardly Lion of Oz
s: Notta and Bob Up, two cowardly lion hunters, travel through the forest toward the Emerald City under Mustafa's orders, hunt the Cowardly Lion, eat supplies, sleep, and reach the Kingdom of Doorways.

l: The Seven Doors, The Cowardly Lion of Oz
s: The Seven Doors are seven heavy oak doors in the wall of the Kingdom of Doorways, each with a brass plate. Only one is right. Their plates give varied warnings, instructions, and identities, including a talking seventh door. Notta and Bob are unsure, try several, and finally enter through the Queen's door.

l: Un, The Cowardly Lion of Oz
s: Un is a rocky, barren skyle: a small island entirely surrounded by clear air and drifting clouds. Restricted to the Uns, it has trees, tree houses, sky wells, and a palace, and is ruled by I-wish-I-was. The Uns live there, grow feathers when something unish happens, and do not work, instead wishing, fishing, and fighting. Visitors fish from its edge until the Uns attack them at night. A good Un hides in a cave after unkind treatment.

l: Flyaboutabus, The Cowardly Lion of Oz
s: Flyaboutabus is the royal flying bus and the only way to leave Un. An immense hollowed-out goose-shaped machine, it has seats, feather wheels, a steering wheel that turns the goose head, a front lever, and buttons controlling speed, direction, altitude, stopping, and landing. Tied to a tree near the palace, it is seized by Notta, Bob, the Cowardly Lion, and Nickadoodle; when its rope is cut, it rises, and Nick uses the loose lever to steady it though they do not know how to descend. It later lands in a field, then flies over the Munchkin country until a storm fills it with water, slows its wheels, and causes a crash. Drained and dried, it continues toward the strange city. In the Preservatory it breaks a Preserve's jar, its controls are crushed by Imperial Squawmos, and only the Up! button remains usable. It rises, strikes a small day star, and hangs from it by a feather wheel.

l: Crunch, The Cowardly Lion of Oz
s: Crunch is a roughly hewn Stone Man, also called the Stone Giant, about three times the size of an ordinary man and made from a huge block of granite. Created in the stone age to decorate a cave, he was buried there for centuries after a landslide until Wam excavated him and gave him life, brains, and magic through magic powder. He lives near Emerald City on an isolated mountain and rescues Notta Bit More and the Cowardly Lion after their fall. Crunch joins the Cowardly Lion’s journey to Mudge, grows fond of him, and promises to help him against Mustafa. Because he is stone, he never tires, travels three times as fast as an ordinary flesh-and-bone man, and cannot break his promise. He carries the lion to Mudge while intending to use a secret transformation trick to make him courageous and keep him forever. At Mudge, he allows Mustafa’s Guards to capture the lion, confronts Mustafa’s attacking lions, and turns 9,999 of them to stone. He enters the enclosure, throws aside stone lions to find the Cowardly Lion, and tries to take him away. However, after petrifying the Cowardly Lion, Glinda and the Wizard of Oz strip Crunch of his power to move, leaving him a statue.
